audit.whatIsWrong: The chart reads Darius / Darius / Skill / Darius / Skill / Darius / Darius, but whys[2] says 'Level 3 E Apprehend cancels his dashes and Windwall can't stop your melee trade', whys[4] says 'Level 6 R executes through his squishy pre-item frame with no defensive counter', and whys[6] says 'Late, Yasuo's crit spike, kiting and dive setup ... flip the matchup to him'. content.late and spikes[3] both say Yasuo takes over after his first crit item.
audit.why: Levels 3 and 6 are the two stages the entry itself calls one-sided in Darius's favour, and the chart marks both Skill; the two-item stage is the one stage every prose field gives to Yasuo, and the chart marks it Darius. The packet chart is Darius x6 then Yasuo at a 54.78% win rate over 6240 games — the largest sample in the slice — and it matches all seven whys.
audit.corrected: win[2] and win[4] to Darius, win[6] to Yasuo, in both layers as one group with ratings realigned.
sources: internal contradiction with whys[2], whys[4], whys[6] and content.late

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 phase text carries the LaTeX fragment 'R = d + a \times Stacks'. Last Breath is described as coming 'online' at 6 with no cooldown anywhere, and the late-game spike is written as 'IE/Shieldbow ... and a Berserker's tempo'.
audit.why: Last Breath is 70/50/30 — the rank-1 miss costs him over a minute and the rank-3 version comes back in half a minute. That collapse from 70s to 30s IS the late-game spike the entry is trying to describe, and it is a fact from the kit rather than a guess about which crit item is currently meta.
audit.corrected: Plain-language Level 6 text plus 70s/30s written into the phases, spikes, breakdown.cooldowns and whys; named items replaced with 'crit items'.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[0] says 'Fight in the wave where his Q sweetspot and E-dashes are limited' and spikes[0] says 'walk up under minions', while the full layer's own tldr says the opposite: 'fight away from massive allied minion waves to restrict his dashes'. content.late says 'Windwall eats your engage' and spikes[2] says Yasuo 'needs a full Windwall dodge' to survive. content.early says he has 'no shield until he stacks Q'.
audit.why: Three separate errors. (1) Sweeping Blade 'dashes through target enemy' — your own minion wave is the thing he dashes through, so standing in it hands him mobility, and the content layer tells the player to do exactly that while the full layer tells him not to. (2) Wind Wall 'blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds' and Darius's kit file carries no projectile flag on any ability — Decimate, Apprehend and Noxian Guillotine all pass straight through, so it can neither eat your engage nor be a thing he must 'dodge' with. (3) The shield is Way of the Wanderer: 'Yasuo builds toward a shield whenever he is moving' — Steel Tempest stacks have nothing to do with it. What Steel Tempest stacks do is arm the whirlwind: 'At 2 stacks, Steel Tempest fires a whirlwind that knocks Airborne', and Last Breath 'Blinks to an Airborne enemy champion' — so the whirlwind is the only thing in the lane that lets his ultimate exist.
audit.corrected: The wave advice made consistent with the tldr, Wind Wall stated as harmless against a projectile-free kit, the shield attributed to Flow, and the whirlwind named as the gate on Last Breath.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns gives Last Breath no number and Apprehend only 'Long early cooldown'.
audit.why: Last Breath 70s at rank 1 versus 30s at rank 3 is the single largest swing in this matchup, Wind Wall is 25s falling to 17s, and Apprehend is 26s falling to 16s. Without them the block says nothing a player can time.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with the real cooldowns and the airborne requirement on Last Breath.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing says Sweeping Blade cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds.
audit.why: Riot's text says exactly that. It means Yasuo cannot chain-dash off you repeatedly — once he has gone through you, he needs a different unit, which is why an empty lane strands him.

notes: Kit-flag false positive: yasuo.json tags Wind Wall (W) with 'terrain: creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes'. Riot's own text is 'Creates a moving wall that blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds' — it blocks projectiles, not movement, and nothing in this matchup was written on the strength of that flag. The projectile point is decided by darius.json's kitFlags, which contains no projectile entry at all: Decimate is a swing, Apprehend is a hook-sweep and Noxian Guillotine is a leap, so Wind Wall has no target in this lane. Steel Tempest's 4s cooldown is the base value in Riot's data; it is reduced by attack speed in game, which is not in the kit file, so no line claims a specific in-fight cadence for it. No yasuo__darius.json mirror existed when this was written. breakdown.difficulty says 'Overall difficulty: 7.5/10' while diffRating and report[13] say 5.5/10 — champion-wide boilerplate mismatch, not touched. This entry's breakdown.wave is the shorter, clean variant rather than the PDF run-on seen elsewhere on Darius.
